s: A fifty-course, multi-hour dinner staged beneath a planetarium dome inside a former naval scenery workshop on Copenhagen's Refshaleøen docklands.
w: Chef Rasmus Munk opened the current 2,200-square-metre Alchemist in 2019 inside a converted Royal Danish Theatre scenery workshop on the former naval island of Refshaleøen, expanding on a fifteen-seat original he had run since 2015. The kitchen serves up to fifty 'impressions' across four to six hours under a planetarium dome, paired with commentary on sustainability and consumption.

s: A Bornholm-rooted tasting menu split between a summer 'growing' season and a winter 'preservation' season, served behind a brick-red door in Christianshavn.
w: Chef Nicolai Nørregaard, raised on the Baltic island of Bornholm, opened Kadeau Copenhagen in 2011 as the city sibling to the original Kadeau on Bornholm, co-founded in 2007. The restaurant moved to its Wildersgade address in Christianshavn in 2015, building its cooking around foraged, preserved and home-grown Bornholm ingredients.
_facts: Three Michelin stars as of the 2026 Nordic Guide
Sister restaurant to the original Kadeau on Bornholm

s: A three-Michelin-star dinner in a converted 19th-century Norrmalm townhouse that opens with a bell at the door and an aperitif in a top-floor lounge.
w: Björn Frantzén opened the restaurant in 2008 with pastry chef Daniel Lindeberg, taking sole ownership and renaming it Frantzén in 2013. In 2016 it relocated to a 19th-century townhouse on Klara Norra Kyrkogata, where guests ring a bell to enter and take an aperitif upstairs before moving to a counter-seating dining room. It became the first Swedish restaurant to hold three Michelin stars in 2018.
_facts: Three Michelin stars since 2018 -- first Swedish restaurant to achieve this

s: A roughly fifteen-course, nose-to-tail tasting menu served on a hilltop former farm above the Baltic Sea between Skillinge and Brantevik.
w: Chef Daniel Berlin opened Vyn on 25 October 2023 on a converted hillside farm near Gislövshammar, on Sweden's Österlen coast, combining a formal restaurant and wine bar with a boutique hotel overlooking the sea. The roughly fifteen-course menu is built nose-to-tail from ingredients foraged, grown and hunted along the surrounding shoreline and farmland.

s: A glass-walled pavilion inside the Stadtpark where Austrian produce is pushed through the discipline of French technique.
w: Heinz and Birgit Reitbauer have run Steirereck as a family restaurant for two decades, in a pavilion set inside Vienna's Stadtpark. In January 2025 it became one of only two restaurants in Austria to hold three Michelin stars, having appeared on the World's 50 Best Restaurants list every year since 2009. Its rooftop garden supplies rare herbs.
_facts: Chef Heinz Reitbauer with wife Birgit
On World's 50 Best every year since 2009

s: A Chiado dining room, steps from a convent ruined in the 1755 earthquake, where Portuguese classics are taken apart and reassembled.
w: Chef José Avillez took over Belcanto in 2012, continuing a restaurant that has occupied Rua Serpa Pinto since 1958. The kitchen revisits Portuguese gastronomy -- its ingredients, textures and history -- and currently holds two Michelin stars, alongside a spot on the World's 50 Best list.

s: A Maxvorstadt dining room near Königsplatz where a chef who left one three-star kitchen built another from scratch in six months.
w: Jan Hartwig opened his eponymous restaurant JAN on Luisenstraße in October 2022, after years running the kitchen at Atelier. Michelin awarded it three stars in its 2023 guide, roughly six months after opening -- inspectors cited his command of craft and technique working at the meeting point of French technique and German classics.

s: A Josefstadt pizzeria where an Apulian-born chef bakes Neapolitan dough for ninety seconds at nearly 500 degrees.
w: Via Toledo Enopizzeria, run by chef Francesco Calò from Apulia, sits on Laudongasse in Vienna's 8th district. Its wood-fired oven bakes Neapolitan-style pizzas at around 485°C for 60 to 90 seconds; its 'Nero di Marinara' pizza was named best pizza in Europe at the 2024 50 Top Pizza Europe Awards.
_facts: 'Nero di Marinara' won best pizza in Europe, 2024

s: A nine-pizza menu and a visible wood-fired oven in a narrow Oud-West storefront, run on long-fermented dough and a blend of Italian and Dutch flours.
w: Opened in 2019 by chef Vincenzo Onnembo with entrepreneur Limau Chen, nNea reworks Neapolitan pizza with slow fermentation and a deliberately high, airy crust. It has repeatedly placed among the top pizzerias in Europe on the 50 Top Pizza list and holds three spicchi from Gambero Rosso.
_facts: Founded 2019 by Vincenzo Onnembo and Limau Chen
Top-ranked pizzeria in the Netherlands on 50 Top Pizza multiple years

s: Fifty seats around a stone oven in the redeveloped Carlsberg brewery district, built entirely around a house sourdough starter fermented for over a day.
w: Founded in 2019 by Sicilian pizzaiolo Giuseppe Oliva, who learned pizza at Bæst, Surt bakes its pizzas from a daily-fed sourdough starter left to ferment 30-35 hours. Toppings mix Danish and organic Italian ingredients, and the room seats only fifty around a stone oven built on-site.
_facts: Founded 2019 by Giuseppe Oliva (previously at Bæst)
Set in the historic Carlsberg brewing district

s: The Wipkingen storefront once known as da PONE, still turning out AVPN-certified Neapolitan pizza under new ownership since late 2023.
w: Formerly da PONE, the pizzeria at Hönggerstrasse 43 was taken over and renamed DA NOI by owner Marco Rampinelli in autumn 2023, keeping the same address and Neapolitan-style pizza program certified by the Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana. Under the da PONE name the address was named Switzerland's top pizzeria and placed among Europe's best on the 50 Top Pizza list.
_facts: Renamed from da PONE to DA NOI, autumn 2023
Named Switzerland's best pizzeria (as da PONE), 2024

s: A decade-old natural-wine-and-pizza room in the Sibirien corner of Vasastan, where wood-fired pies share the counter with rotating small plates.
w: Babette opened roughly a decade ago on Roslagsgatan as one of Stockholm's first bars to pair wood-fired, Italian-leaning pizza with a natural wine list. The kitchen builds pizzas around ingredients like nduja and pumpkin, alongside small plates such as coppa with melon and chilli. It holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand.
_facts: One of Stockholm's earliest natural-wine-and-pizza bars

s: A Calabrian-run Neapolitan pizzeria in Saint-Josse where the dough rests two full days before it ever meets the 450-degree oven.
w: Run by the Leone family, La Piola Pizza turns out strictly Neapolitan pies from a wood-fired oven kept at roughly 450°C. The dough ferments 48 hours on organic flour and natural yeast, finished with buffalo ricotta on the crust. In the 2026 edition of 50 Top Pizza Europe it placed 15th, the highest ranking of any pizzeria in Belgium.
_facts: Run by the Leone family, Calabrian roots
Ranked 15th, 50 Top Pizza Europe 2026 -- top in Belgium

s: A Nepalese chef's Neapolitan pizzeria in Lisbon, its oven leafed in gold and assembled from parts shipped over from Naples.
w: Opened in 2014 by chef Tanka Sapkota, Forno d'Oro bakes AVPN-certified Neapolitan pizza from a wood-fired oven lined with gold leaf. The dough ferments for 36 hours, and alongside San Marzano tomatoes and buffalo mozzarella the kitchen works in Portuguese ingredients such as Serra da Estrela cheese. It is the only Portuguese restaurant to appear on the 50 Top Pizza World ranking.
_facts: Only Portuguese restaurant on 50 Top Pizza World list

s: A Sardinian-run pizzeria and Italian deli near Bratislava's Blumentál, where Neapolitan pies share a menu with culurgiones and seadas.
w: Opened in December 2017 by Sardinian chef and owner Andrea Ena, U Taliana pairs a Neapolitan-style pizzeria with a small Italian delicatessen and pastry counter. Alongside the pizza, the kitchen makes handmade pasta and Sardinian specialties such as culurgiones and seadas. It appeared in the 50 Top Pizza Europe rankings, placing 47th in the 2023 edition.

s: A single-focus Neapolitan pizzeria in a centuries-old inn building directly across from Fürth's town hall.
w: Since 2023, chef and owner Gaspare Squitieri has run Pizza Zulu from the historic Gasthof Schwarzes Kreuz building opposite Fürth's Rathaus, serving only Neapolitan-style pizza built on long-fermented dough and San Marzano tomatoes. The 50 Top Pizza guide named it the best pizzeria in Germany multiple years running.
_facts: Named best pizzeria in Germany, 50 Top Pizza, multiple years
In the historic Gasthof Schwarzes Kreuz, opposite the Rathaus

s: Three Michelin stars in a converted West Loop garage, the menu dictated week to week by a chef-couple's own farm.
w: John Shields and Karen Urie Shields run the tasting counter around whatever came off their farm outside Chicago that morning, down to the eggs and root vegetables. In 2026 it became the first Chicago restaurant named No. 1 on North America's 50 Best Restaurants list.
_facts: Three Michelin stars, Chicago's only 3-star restaurant
Chefs John Shields and Karen Urie Shields

s: A French-inflected neighbourhood bistro from the Elske chefs next door, named after an in-house joke that stuck.
w: David and Anna Posey opened Creepies in late 2025 as the looser, more Midwestern-accented sibling to their Michelin-starred Elske around the corner, with checkerboard tile floors and stone-and-wood walls. The kitchen runs French bistro staples alongside dishes like steamed halibut with sauce homard.
_facts: Opened West Loop, late 2025, David and Anna Posey (also of Elske)

s: A 24-hour-diner-styled bar-restaurant whose thin, griddled double cheeseburger under a fried egg is routinely called the best in the country.
w: Brendan Sodikoff opened Au Cheval in 2012, before the West Loop's restaurant row fully formed around it. The burger -- two griddled patties, American cheese, Dijonnaise, a fried egg on request -- has since topped best-burger lists at Food Network, Eater, and Business Insider. No reservations for the main dining room.
_facts: Signature double cheeseburger named a top U.S. burger by multiple outlets

s: A fine-dining Italian room built into a 19th-century brick barn that once stabled horses for the Mount Adams incline railway.
w: Nicola Pietoso opened the restaurant in 1996 inside the old incline-trolley barn on the edge of Over-the-Rhine; his son Cristian now runs it, having added second-floor seating and expanded the wine cellar. The menu runs contemporary northern Italian, anchored by a private Riserva wine room downstairs.
_facts: Opened 1996 by Nicola Pietoso; now run by son Cristian
Housed in a former incline-railway horse barn

s: The 1956 walk-up burger stand -- red-and-white tile, no drive-through -- that grew into a chain obsessive enough to win a national quality award.
w: Fred 'Pal' Barger opened this squat, cantilever-roofed stand on Revere Street in 1956, and it still runs as a walk-up counter with no drive-through, unlike every Pal's built after it. The chain it launched became the only restaurant company to win the Malcolm Baldrige National Quality Award.
_facts: Opened 1956 by Fred 'Pal' Barger; original building still operating
No drive-through, unlike later Pal's locations
Only restaurant company to win the Malcolm Baldrige National Quality Award
